note: Humour pop culture de Card Hustle. Règles d'écriture : allusions reconnaissables, jamais de réplique culte recopiée mot pour mot, pas de nom de personnage ou de marque dans le texte dit (le champ 'reference' sert seulement à l'audit). Chaque réplique a un public (âge), des goûts (ce que le personnage connaît) et une intensité (1 = clin d'œil discret, 2 = blague franche, 3 = gros gag) ; le directeur d'humour décide si et quand elle sort.

repliques.texte: Oh, there’s a whole side quest. It ends with me fetching ten mushrooms for nobody.
That story has three endings. Depends on what dialogue option you pick.
The lore runs deep. Like, collect-every-scattered-diary-page deep.
Previously, on This Town…
It’s a long story. Like, extended-edition-with-appendices long.
I’d tell you, but then the plot twist wouldn’t hit as hard.
That’s canon. Everything after that is fan theory.
Okay, but first you need the context. And the context needs context.
The full story unlocks at friendship level three.
repliques.reference: jauges d'amitié des simulations de vie

repliques.texte: My grandson says it ‘has lore’. I think that means it’s complicated.
In this house we call that a rare drop. As in, it rarely happens and then drops on you.
There’s more, but you have to watch until after the credits.
Achievement unlocked: actually listening.
Glad to help. Consider it a free tutorial.
Tip of the day: never trust a crate in a game, or a free sample at the market.
You’re welcome. Your quest log has been updated.
Happy to help. I’m basically the friendly shopkeeper in the first village.
Anytime. Wisdom: plus one.
No problem. My granddaughter would say I ‘carried’. I carried groceries mostly.
Thanks. Here’s hoping today doesn’t have a final boss.
You too. May your loading screens be short.
Thanks. I’ll save my progress just in case.
Thanks. Everything is fine. That’s what the dog in the burning room said too.
repliques.reference: chien dans la pièce en feu

repliques.texte: You too. Main character energy, okay?
Honestly? My stamina bar is flashing red.
Let’s just say my needs bars are all orange.
repliques.reference: jauges de besoins des simulations de vie

repliques.texte: It’s fine. Everything is fine. Small fire, very calm dog.
repliques.reference: chien dans la pièce en feu

repliques.texte: Today felt like a level where you can’t pause.
I died a few times, but I respawned at the coffee machine.
Tired. Like a hero after the training montage, minus the muscles.
Rough day. The kids would say it was ‘an emotional damage situation’. I just say Tuesday.
I’m okay. No thoughts, head empty, just vibes.
Sure. Party member joined.
Another time. Let’s say I’ll be at the same spot, same hour, like a well-scripted villager.
Co-op mode? Sure. You hold the bags.
See you. Don’t forget to save.
Bye! I’ll be right here, standing in the exact same spot. As one does.
Go on. Your quest marker is blinking.
Later. Don’t fast-travel into a wall.
Take care. Heading out alone? Here, take a snack. Every hero starts with one item.
repliques.reference: allusion au vieil homme de la grotte

repliques.texte: See you. I’ll pretend this conversation never happened, spy-movie style.
Bye. Touch some grass on the way, it’s free.
Off you go. My grandson says ‘GG’. I believe it means good luck.
That joke needed a patch before release.
Critical miss.
Roll for charisma. Oh. Oh no.
Skill issue. Comedy skill, specifically.
I can hear the sitcom laugh track refusing to play.
That one’s getting a one-star review.
Common rarity. Heavily played.
You’re grinding that joke like it’s going to level up.
Interesting strategy. The crowd remains unconvinced.
This is your villain origin story, isn’t it?
Follow the fountain. Everything here is one fast-travel point.
By the square. If you reach the edge of the map, you went too far.

receptions.note: Réaction d'un personnage quand le joueur choisit un ton joueur ou absurde, selon son style d'humour. 'rit' si le personnage aime ce genre de blague, 'poli' sinon, 'plat' quand ce n'est vraiment pas le moment (émotion négative, négociation tendue).

rit: Okay, that was decent. Don’t let it go to your head.
Ha. Fine. One point to you.
poli: I’m laughing on the inside. Deep inside.
Somebody write that down. Then lose it.
I see what you did there. I’m choosing not to react.
plat: Let’s keep it serious for a minute.

poli: Heh, you’re in a mood today.

rit: Hahaha! Wait, why is it funny? Hahaha!
poli: I don’t get it but okay!

rit: Oh, I’m telling that one at dinner.
That’s a good one, I’ll steal it.
poli: You’re in a good mood today.

rit: Ha! Nice reference. I’m counting it.
poli: I get the reference. I just don’t respect it.
Mid, but I see the effort.
Two out of five stars. Generous.

rit: Ha! That’s one of those internet jokes, isn’t it? I love those.
Oh, you young people and your bits!
Ha! You remind me of my brother. He was trouble too.
Oh, that’s a good one. I won’t remember it, but it’s good.
poli: I’ll laugh once my grandson explains it.
Is that a meme? It feels like a meme.

etapes.texte: Six ducks refused to leave the crosswalk this morning. Traffic stopped. The ducks did not care.
The ducks are back. One of them stared at me like I owed it money.
The ducks now cross in formation. I think they have a leader. I think it has a plan.
Final report on the ducks: they won. We put up a sign. They ignore the sign.

running_gags.titre: La Bourse de Tyler et Noah

etapes.texte: Noah and I opened a trading desk. It’s a bench, but it’s a professional bench.
Market update: shiny dragons are up two juice boxes. Bugs are down. Bugs are always down.
We had a crash. Mason traded a holo for a dinosaur sticker. Noah needs a minute.
We recovered! The market loves dinosaurs now. Mason is a genius. Or lucky. Noah says lucky.
Try the sauce. Don’t comment on the sauce. Just try the sauce.
Mike says his barbecue sauce is better. Mike is wrong, and Mike knows it.
The recipe is locked in a safe. The safe is locked in my head. My head is locked to Mike.
Fine. One secret ingredient. It’s patience. And a lot of paprika. Mostly paprika.
Has anyone seen my good wrench? Not the other good wrench. The good one.
Jamie labeled every tool in the shed. Every single one. Even the label maker has a label.
Found the wrench. It was in my hand. For two days. Don’t tell Carol.
Doug lent the wrench again. We’re starting a tracking system. It has a spreadsheet and a prayer.
I averaged every price this month. The average is lying, but consistently.
Ben says I forgot condition again. My spreadsheet has feelings now. Column G is called Regret.
I added a column for language. Then one for ‘vibes’. Ben is concerned.
The spreadsheet crashed. I stared at it like the end of a sad movie. It was beautiful.
That water tower has incredible lighting at six. I’ve taken two hundred photos.
Antonio says he helped build it. He also says he built half the town. I’m starting to believe him.
I think the water tower is the town’s final boss. Nobody has seen the top.
Antonio took me up. The top has a chair, a thermos and a 1983 newspaper. Legend confirmed.
The bus leaves at 8:10. Not 8:11. The bus is not a negotiation.
Someone asked me to wait one minute. I said: this is a bus, not a loading screen.
Gloria says I’m strict. Gloria once left the mayor at a bus stop. In the rain. On his birthday.
Stalls open at seven. Not seven-ish. Seven. I printed it in bold.
I added rule fourteen: no haggling with a dramatic speech about destiny. You know who you are.
Patricia contradicted me in front of everyone. She was right. That’s not the point. The point is the rules.
